featured_reviews.name: LeLe
featured_reviews.review_text: Highly recommend this outstanding tour! Friends of mine did a food tour with Arpan and liked it so much they booked a walking tour with him for the next day and asked me to join. Arpan took us to interesting places, some of which you wouldn't find in a tour guide and he knew a lot to tell about them, you get to meet locals and hardly see any other tourists. Arpan is super funny and smart, he speaks excellent English and has very reasonable prices for his tours. If I come back to Mumbai I'll definitely do a tour with him again.

featured_reviews.name: Sas Mac
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Mumbai as a solo female traveller in May 2019 with 2 nights booked not knowing anyone or much about the city. I saw Bombay walks advertised at my hostel and thought I would check it out for the evening to introduce me to the city. I ended up staying and extra night and booking a tour with Arpan everyday as I had so much fun and made my way around the city like a local on the trains, tuk tuks and walking. I ate street food and was shown the history of Mumbai. Arpan was fun, respectable and knowledgable about Mumbai and India. He gave me help with the rest of my trip, recomending Udaipur and booking my flights for my. He also has great insite into hostels throughout the country!

Great guy, couldn't recommend him more

featured_reviews.name: Sam Shapiro
featured_reviews.review_text: Arpan was great- he was very knowledgeable about the history of India and of the places he took us. He began by providing us with context for everywhere we were going to go that day, showing us on a map what the route would look like and why he chose the places he was taking us to. Each place he took us was very interesting and, as promised, slightly different than what you may find from a more generic tour. He was great at answering questions, and ended the tour with a discussion with the group about what it’s like to grow up in India.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

featured_reviews.name: Moni K.
featured_reviews.review_text: Thanks to Bombay Walks Mumbay became the highlight of my India trip! Arpan took me to hidden places to give me an authentic insight to the city and its lifestyle and it was just amazing. I experienced street food, local markets and cozy bars with him. As a female solo traveller i never felt unsafe during my time with Arpan. He is such a perfect guide who speaks clear english and takes care of u all of the time. Really highly recommendable, also for female travellers!

featured_reviews.name: Tonya Lenox
featured_reviews.review_text:
Simply amazing. It was our last tour of our trip but easily our favorite one!  I wish he could’ve done all our tours through India! And such a good price.
He was our only tour guide who did not push us to purchase things or leave a review. He cared more about us truly having a good experience and understanding of his country.
He had a lot of knowledge of so many different aspects of not only the locations he showed us but also could answer a lot of questions we had about India in general as well. He was timely, communicated easily and most importantly had a great mix of fun and truth on the tour. Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: sheena patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai, it’s a city I’ve ‘visited’ many times however I wouldn’t say I had experienced the localities until I booked myself on the fabulous walking tour with Arpan. Bombay walks allowed tourists to experience the pockets of the city in detail and depth.

Arpan is extremely knowledgable about the various different neighbourhoods of mumbai. The tour takes you through various areas of the crazy city. He will point out all the landmarks, highlights and he definitely knows some of mumbai’s best hidden coffee spots😉.

You can ask him a million questions and he will patiently give you all the answers.
Leaving you in awe of how Mumbai comes together chaotically.

The tour had been designed to give tourists like myself a taster of this metro. I would highly recommend it! Our bilingual Arpan can share his stories in English, Hindi, Marathi and Marwari :)

I look forward to returning to Mumbai soon  and participating in many other walks!

featured_reviews.name: Baker Mags
featured_reviews.review_text:
Wonderful experience!

Arpan is friendly and full of knowledge.
Would have not been able to experience the beautiful churches, streets, food and art of Bandra without his support. One should definately opt for this walking tour.

Highly recommended.

All the best!
-Megha

name: South Mumbai Heritage Walk by MDT
description:
The Mumbai Heritage Walk is a great way to experience the city’s vibrant culture and rich history.
Mumbai Heritage Walk is probably known as the ‘dream city’ and rightly so the city is indeed like a beautiful, magnificent dream. Old Mumbai is the part of Mumbai that represents its heritage and history. Reflecting on the time of Colonial era, the area is studded with numerous tourist attractions. From Chhatrapati Shivaji terminus to the ‘White town’ to the University library to the magnificent Marine drive, the city has so many spectacular attractions that one can never miss. Explore all these places of Old Mumbai and many more with this heritage walk tour.

Walking tours expose many residents and visitors to the structures.

featured_reviews.name: Darren DSouza
featured_reviews.review_text:
The long promenade, sea breeze, and open space make it perfect for evening walks. There’s plenty of seating, play areas for kids, skating spots, and it’s also great for jogging.

There are restaurants and cafes nearby too, which makes it easy to spend a couple of hours here without feeling rushed. Definitely one of a refreshing spots in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text: Carter Road Promenade in Bandra is a beautiful seaside escape and one of Mumbai’s most loved walking spots. The long, well-laid promenade runs alongside the sea, offering stunning sunset views and a calming breeze, especially in the evenings. It is generally quite clean and well maintained, with plenty of benches to sit and relax while enjoying the view. Weekends can get crowded with walkers, joggers, families, and pet owners, but the vibe remains pleasant. Thankfully, there are no hawkers disturbing the space. However, the area seriously needs more decent, clean public toilets to improve the overall experience.

featured_reviews.name: Karan Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
They’ve added a section for skate park and boards. Kids and youngsters and skate enthusiasts seem to love it. I think it could do more good with a little more upkeep from authorities.

They’ve added elements across the promenade to enhance its charm and appeal but it could do with some regular and serious maintenance & upkeep.

Also a majority of pet peeps who regularly walk their dogs out here aren’t too big on leashes ( you can choose to do with this information / opinion as you like). Great spot to interact with doggos.

A few people have pointed out that the dog park isn’t exactly the best or safe environment for dogs to play on account of them encountering some health issues on odd occasions.

featured_reviews.name: Shakeel Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
This 1.5 km long promenede along the black stone beaches of Khar-Danda shores is a very good place for walkers n joggers, not for runners.

Along the long narrow promenede, you see famous mangroves reserved forest, gym, dogs park, kids park, skating rink, koli (sea) food corner n wider sitting space overseeing beautiful view of sea n under construction Carter connector to upcoming Versova-Bandra Sea Link (VBSL) coastal road project.

Towards the North, u can smell drying fish odour ( ;>) coming from Danda Koliwada n morning releiving scenes.

Towards the South, if you cross under construction Carter bridge, you reach to Joggers Park which is separately reviewed.

A latest edition to this Promenade is sea food eatery stalls made at the North end at Khar Danda. Run by local fishermen community women, their classic savours are worth challenging Khau Galli costly restraurants opposite side.

See review of "Khar Danda Koli Savour" also.

review_photos.caption: Sea-food festival at every Friday-Saturday-Sunday at this end of promenade. Koli savours.

featured_reviews.name: Sharad Khandelwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Its just so peaceful and serene to have a walk here. We decided to spent some us time bere on New Years instead of crowded places and it was a bliss!
There are ample places to sit and enjoy the sunset and the sea. There's a park for kids along with a dog park too!
Its just mesmerizing to see the sunset here and spent time with your loved ones and friends. Or just plain and simple have a hearty walk alongside the sea!

featured_reviews.name: Advocate Rita Kapur
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a delight for early morning walkers to see hundreds of school  kids every Sunday morning happily  doing their studies along  the Carter road seaside  promenade.  Kids are helped for any difficulties they face in their studies and are made to understand the importance & need for education and self-sufficiency. Children are also served  breakfast  thereafter.  This initiative is of the NGO NAVJYOT in Mumbai and is personally overseen by  senior decades long dedicated women volunteers who are there on the spot  every Sunday morn.
Some photos of these happy kids facing the amazing Arabian Sea. An eye opener for sure.

featured_reviews.name: Soham Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a must visit, especially if you're a couple. It's approximately 1-1.5 km long street by the sea, perpendicular to it is a row of cafés. It has a lot of benches, just by the sea, where you can sit and enjoy the beauty of the sea. It's moderately crowded and often has policeman standing guard. Pick something up to drink and munch on from the cafe and sit by the sea on one of the benches and enjoy the sunset. You'll thank me for the wonderful time you'll have. There's one particular bench right on the rocks which is just perfect, if you can find it, you'll enjoy it even more.

name: IanWalksMumbai
description:
IanWalksMumbai is your invitation to discover the city the way Ian did—on foot, with curiosity, humor, and a healthy respect for potholes. Expect vivid histories, unexpected detours, and probably a snack stop or three. You won’t just see Mumbai—you’ll feel it, taste it, laugh with it… and maybe get a little lost with Ian (on purpose).

Ready to walk? Let’s go.

featured_reviews.name: Cassandra R
featured_reviews.review_text: I booked a full day tour with Ian and couldn’t have had a better guide to show me all over Mumbai. He was on time, curated my experience to my tastes, so full of information, and a welcoming host. He met me at my hotel, arranged for a driver, sweated in 43°, and never slowed down. I tasted food safely, felt safe as a solo woman traveler, never felt forced into buying anything I didn’t. It was truly an experience of a lifetime and I’m so very grateful. Thank you Ian!

featured_reviews.name: An G
featured_reviews.review_text:
We went for a heritage walk in CSMT with Ian late-September, and it was a blast!

He’s energetic, well-informed and convivial!

The walk took about 2 hours — wherein we explored the exterior and interior architectural aspects of the iconic train station. Throughout the walk, Ian regaled us with stories of historical significance, and even quizzed us a bit along the way! It was very engaging.

We made a stop at the train museum inside the station - a modest setup with a LOT of paraphernalia for rail transport enthusiasts!

Before we did this walk - We really didn’t know how much the station had to offer, despite living in Mumbai for some time now.

Walks like these are a lovely way to get acquainted with the city. An experience made all the richer with an enthusiastic and passionate guide like Ian!

We look forward to joining him for another heritage walk sometime! Thank you for a memorable time.

featured_reviews.name: Manmohan Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Really enjoyed the CSMT UNESCO World Heritage Tour! Ian was an amazing guide super friendly and knew so many cool facts about the place. The way he explained the history and little details made it really interesting. Had a great time exploring and learning. Totally worth it! 😊

featured_reviews.name: Obada
featured_reviews.review_text: We took an evening tour fir the south of Mumbai. The trip with Ian was very informative, engaging and interesting. Ian has a fun story telling style that makes the tour special. The fact that it's a private free walking tour is really unique and offers a lot of flexibility in terms of the tour's timing and topics in focus. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Rajdeep Maity
featured_reviews.review_text: I've visited CSMT countless times growing up, but I never really understood its architecture until this tour. Seeing it through Ian's explanation changed the entire experience. The way you broke things down made the details easy to follow, and the way you told the stories behind the place kept it engaging instead of feeling like a history lecture. I walked away actually appreciating the structure instead of just passing by it. Overall, the tour was genuinely fun and surprisingly eye-opening

featured_reviews.name: Ananya Nayak
featured_reviews.review_text:
On Saturday, 6th of December I took a tour of CSMT with Ian. When I had booked the tour (available in BMS) I was only interested in the gigantic magnificent buildings. But Ian, made me look and understand them. This person is nostalgic and passionate about the history and buildings. He not only recites the history, he connects the dots to the present.

He quizzes you on things, makes it interactive and introspective and is very friendly. He narrates fun incidents happening over different times and isn't afraid to admit that there are few things that he isn't very aware of.

The walk is designed to have a look at almost everything, including a reclusive Railway Museum which isn't other wise opened to the public. He also recommends other tours, areas to explore and much more.

I would definitely recommend this tour.

featured_reviews.name: Krishnan Anantharaman
featured_reviews.review_text: Ian led our tour of CSMT in Mumbai, including areas of the grand railway office building that are off limits to the public. He kept the tour fun and engaging, and covered a LOT of ground in a short time: colonial history, architecture, commerce and all the other influences on this spectacular structure.

featured_reviews.name: Ajit Varma
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a very interesting and informative tour in which the history and architectural aspects of the CSMT building is explained very minutely. There is also a heritage railway museum visit in this having lots of interesting information on past present railway. One can also see working models.
Our tour guide was Mr Ian Fernandes. He is extremely talented and good communicator.
He took special care for senior citizens.
Well priced and value for money tour.
One who is visiting Mumbai should go for this.
We booked on  Bookmy show app .Tour name is "crown jewel of Mumbai inside CSMT".

featured_reviews.name: shoeb sayed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jogger’s Park is one of Mumbai’s most beloved seaside urban parks and jogging spots, nestled at the southern end of Carter Road promenade in Bandra West. It’s a classic example of how community initiative transformed a former garbage dump into a green fitness haven in the early 1990s, thanks largely to local efforts led by Oliver Andrade and support from prominent Mumbai residents — a legacy memorialised by a plaque at the entrance that says “From Sir, With Love.”
Wikipedia

Park Highlights
Scenic jogging tracks: The park features a 400-metre long stretch with a mix of mud, synthetic and paved pathways that suit casual walkers and serious runners alike.

Sea views & fresh air: Its location along the Arabian Sea offers cool breezes and calming views of the water — especially beautiful at sunrise and sunset.
Chalbanjare
Green spaces & gardens: Beyond jogging, there are lush lawns, landscaped paths, benches and shaded spots perfect for relaxation, meditation, or reading.
Chalbanjare
Kid-friendly area: There’s a dedicated children’s play area with swings, slides and soft flooring, making it family-friendly.
The Indian Express

Activities & Atmosphere
Jogger’s Park isn’t just for fitness — it’s a community hub where locals gather for morning runs, evening walks, yoga sessions or simply to meet friends. It’s also known for hosting Mumbai’s first laughter club, a unique wellness activity that began here.

Visitors often enjoy:
Walking or running with sea views
Meditation and casual outdoor workouts
Relaxing on benches overlooking the coast
Family outings with kids in the play area

Practical Info
Timings: Typically open 5:00 AM – 9:00 PM (best early morning and evening).
Whats Hot
Entry: Free to enter since the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) took over maintenance.  
Ticket Fairy
Location: At the end of Carter Road, near landmarks like Otters Club and Bandra’s lively seafront promenade.  
Ticket Fairy
Getting there: Easily reachable by auto/taxi from Bandra Railway Station, or by BEST buses along Carter Road.
Ticket Fairy

Jogger’s Park blends fitness with serenity a rare open space in a bustling city where you can breathe fresh sea air, watch waves crash, and enjoy a peaceful escape without leaving the suburb. Locals and visitors alike cherish it for its history, community vibe, and relaxed seaside ambience.

featured_reviews.name: Prashhant Hatiskar
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited Jogger's Park for the first time, though I had heard about it before. It turned out to be a peaceful and well-maintained place, perfect for a quiet walk or some time outdoors. The atmosphere was calm, making it a great spot to relax and unwind.

featured_reviews.name: Shakeel Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
A nice serene oval garden on the stone beach shores of western coast near Carter road. Fav place for walkers, runners n joggers as well cuz all types of parallel tracks are there. On the left of entry, a very good kids garden is there having all sorts of colorful slides, see-saw, swings n what not. On the right of entry, elders gym is there having parallel bars n other exercise items.
In the mid of garden, small pond is there where u can see duck n Desi chicken in cage. Mid garden part is green also n facilitate yoga enthusiasts. The toilets are always open, but not so hygienic.
A lot of cats also can be seen here as people feed them.
One outer periphery round of this park makes 450m.

featured_reviews.name: Shakeel Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
When u walk along a promenade, distance covered is not important. Important is night colors capture along the Bay of Mahim shore in 1.25 km stretch. BWSL Promenede is a place placed beautifully on the way joining Western Mumbai to Southern Mumbai through magnificent Bandra Worli Sea Link (BWSL). While going to South Mumbai in morning or evening, just take a detour down below on left side before BWSL toll gate n u will be at Promenede on right side adjacent to Asha Bhosle Sargam Udyan. The promenade park opens/ closes at 06-09 a.m. n 05-09 p.m.
Attractive for Joggers, Runners, kids, elderly ppl, romantic couple, broken hearts n photo enthusiasts equally which I m proving thru pics. In this two level park stretch, there r three children parks of different age kids, four animals statues,  two public gyms. two amphitheaters, one basket ball court, uncountable romance sheds n endless retention wall n yes- no toilets.
There r two Balconies protruded in sea, beautiful dates tree witnessing dating couples on retention walls, park curves n geometry, artificial lit trees, beautiful imperial design poles of solar street lightings.
Found this park most beautiful in nights, especially at low tide times when u can see muddy land in various shapes representing a different natural profile in the sea from Meethi River Eastern side. And in the residual waters, beautiful light reflections in sea of Mahim- Dadar-Prabhadevi-Worli side high rise buildings lights.
Don't forget to see marvellous lighting decorations in this promenede from Christmas to Sankranti festival in mid January, which takes this already beautiful park to a totally different level.

featured_reviews.name: Harsh A
featured_reviews.review_text:
I did the Duke's nose sunrise trek with Traver's India, and woah, it was such an incredible experience. The team is professional, competent, and attentive. They're safety focused and actually want you to have a good time.

Here's what my trip was like:

1. I was picked up by their bus at around 11 pm (this was a night trek). The bus was comfortable and all the fellow trekkers were quite spirited, so it was fun.
2. We reached the base village at 3:30 am (i.e. on time)
3. Proper washroom facilities were provided to girls
4. We were given a snack packet and a safety instruction + everyone introduced themselves officially.
5. At 4:15 we began the trek. It was cold and windy, but that didn't bother me because this was my first night trek and I was just too busy with the novelty of the whole thing.
6. The guide-to-paying-customer ratio is 1:5 (3 guides for the total of 15 of us) which is very good and you get a lot of attention if you need help.
7. I had some breathing difficulties because of the cold, so I had to climb slowly. One of the guides stayed behind me at all times instead of moving ahead. I'm very impressed.
8. We reached the top by 5:45 (also on time) and waited for sunrise to come. The team made sure that no one got to close to the edge of the cliff (there were many teenagers in the group so it's good that they were very safety conscious).
9. There was a small temple at the top. You had to remove your shoes to enter. I didn't go here because I was too cold to remove my shoes.
10. At 7:30, we started the descent. We came down via a different route and took many pictures now that the sun was up. This was more enjoyable in my opinion as you can actually see the scenery after the sun is up. Plus the temperature was way better (not freezing).
11. Down in the base village, I was given breakfast (Maggi, poha, and tea and coffee) and I played with the dogs.
12. When we were done, we left for Mumbai in the same bus and I was home by 1 pm.

Here's some of the reasons why I like these guys in particular over other groups:

1. The high guide-to-trekker ratio. You have 1 guide for 5 people, which means you're very safe and taken care of. The "slow people" get a guide too instead of everyone just moving ahead.
2. They kept the group together and coordinated pickup and drops properly. Everything was on schedule and very well managed.
3. They gave me a pillow to sleep on on the bus ride back home.
4. I picked up some bits of the local language (Marathi) from the other trekkers hahahaha

What could have been better:

The only thing I can think of is that the organizers didn't stress the importance of carrying a woolen cap. It was freezing cold on the top with very strong and continuous winds and I didn't have a cap or gloves. Had to make do with tying a towel around my ears (Fortunately, I was carrying a towel!). Although, this can be attributed to my lack of experience because many other trekkers did carry woolen caps and gloves without being told to.

Overall:

I'm very happy and impressed by Travers India and will be going on more treks with them. I'm also very shocked at how cheap/affordable the entire thing was. It literally cost just $20 (I paid a bit less than 1600 Indian Rupees) and included snacks, breakfast, AND transportation to and from the city. Hah.

Getting Married at Mount Mary Church
Mount Mary Church, also known as the Basilica of Our Lady of the Mount, is a beautiful Roman Catholic church and a popular wedding venue. Here are the general steps involved in getting married there:
* Contact the Church: Get in touch with the church office well in advance (at least 6 months) to inquire about their wedding procedures, availability of dates, and required documents. You'll likely need to meet with the parish priest.
* Pre-Cana Course:  Most Catholic churches require couples to attend a pre-marital counseling course (often called Pre-Cana). This helps prepare you for marriage and covers topics like communication, finances, and family life.
* Necessary Documents:  You'll need to provide documents like:
* Baptism certificates
* Confirmation certificates
* Marriage license (if applicable)
* No objection certificate from your parish priest (if you're not from that parish)
* Banns of Marriage: The church will announce your intention to marry (called "banns") for three consecutive Sundays. This is to ensure there are no canonical impediments to your marriage.
* Meeting with the Priest: You'll have meetings with the priest to discuss the wedding ceremony, your vows, and any specific requests you may have.
* Wedding Rehearsal:  A rehearsal is usually held a day or two before the wedding to ensure everything runs smoothly.
* Wedding Day:  The wedding ceremony will typically include a Mass, exchange of vows, and blessings.
Important Notes:
* Booking:  Since Mount Mary is a popular church, book your wedding date well in advance, especially if you're planning to get married during peak season.
* Decorations: The church may have restrictions on decorations, so discuss this with them beforehand.
* Photography:  Check if there are any specific rules regarding photography or videography during the ceremony.
* Donations:  There may be a customary donation to the church for the use of the facilities.
Remember: These are general guidelines. It's crucial to contact Mount Mary Church directly to get the most accurate and up-to-date information on their wedding requirements and procedures.

featured_reviews.name: Liviu-Alexandru Buftea (Style)
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you found this place, you had a good guide!

I thought it was Portuguese, but it's actually British. Black as the basaltic rock that rises from the sea, Worli Fort gives a great overview of the bay and the city. It features the classic crenelations and ramparts of the 17th century, and guards the golf from the tip of this tongue of land.

The fort now is not officially maintained or "open to the public". In fact, it seems even locals don’t know about it, but my friend brought me here cause she heard it’s nice. It is accessible for explorer types, and is basically left abandoned.

The fort is simply used by people in this neighborhood for storage, hang out, kids play space, etc. Some clothes left out to dry on the sides, and some barrels and stuff in the rooms below.

Here we met a couple of guys from the city, chilling, listening to cool music, they welcomed us to chat.

It smelled of sea salt, soap, garbage, fish and rats, and the breeze brought “fresh” air from the sea.

As a first time visitor in India, I was in culture shock. Seeing everything was kind of like a dreamy, surreal landscape. So I probably romanticized it too much, for the place is a slum surrounded by a garbage dump, and people here have little chance to better their days, but they were happy, kind and curious.

It was an interesting and humbling experience, worth respect.

Shivaji Park is not just a ground — it’s an emotion for every cricket lover. If you really want to watch future superstars of Indian cricket in the making, this is the place to be. On the red soil of this historic ground, you’ll see young kids practicing with full dedication, sweating it out under the sharp Mumbai sun, chasing their dreams with bat and ball in hand.
There’s something special about standing there and watching them play. The sound of leather hitting the bat, coaches shouting instructions, and parents cheering from the side — it all feels raw and real. Many legends, including Sachin Tendulkar, began their journey here, which makes the atmosphere even more inspiring.
The park is huge, so even if you're not into cricket, it’s a perfect place for a peaceful walk or to just sit and relax. In the evening, the cool breeze and open space make it ideal for clearing your mind after a long day.

The 113,000 square metres (28 acres) of open space is renowned as having been a cradle of the game of cricket in India.

featured_reviews.name: Ayaj Deshmukh
featured_reviews.review_text:
🌿 A Majestic Experience at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park
🏞️ Pride of Dadar, Mumbai | A Historic Ground of Courage & Culture 👑🇮🇳
Visiting Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park in Dadar, Mumbai, was a truly memorable, emotional, and inspiring experience for me 💚. This park is not just an open ground—it is a historical landmark that carries the spirit of Maharashtra’s pride, unity, and rich legacy 🌟. The moment I stepped onto this vast green land, I felt a deep sense of respect and belonging 🙏.
The park is named after Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, the great Maratha warrior king who symbolizes bravery, good governance, and Swarajya 👑⚔️. Standing here, I could feel the echoes of history in the air. This ground has witnessed many historic political movements, social gatherings, freedom-related events, and public speeches that shaped modern Maharashtra 🇮🇳📜. Knowing this made my visit even more meaningful and powerful.
As I walked through the park, I noticed people of all ages—children playing, elders walking peacefully, students practicing sports, and groups doing yoga 🏃‍♂️🧘‍♀️. The park beautifully balances history and daily life, showing how the past and present coexist harmoniously 🌸. The lush greenery and open space provide a refreshing escape from the busy city life of Mumbai 🌳🌬️.
One of the most emotional aspects of my visit was realizing that this very ground has been a platform for voices demanding justice, equality, and rights ✊. Many great leaders have addressed the nation from here, making it a silent witness to India’s democratic journey 🗣️📢. Being present at such a historically significant place filled me with pride and responsibility as a citizen 🤍.
The surrounding area reflects Mumbai’s cultural richness, with nearby temples, roads filled with local life, and a strong sense of Maharashtrian identity 🎭🪔. The park stands as a reminder that public spaces can unite people beyond caste, religion, and background, just like the ideals of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj himself 🤝.
As the evening breeze touched my face and the sky slowly changed colors 🌅, I felt calm yet energized. This place doesn’t just relax the body—it awakens the soul. It teaches us discipline, unity, and respect for our roots 🌱.
In conclusion, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Park is more than a park—it is a living chapter of Indian history 🏞️📖. Every visit deepens respect for our heritage and inspires us to live with courage, integrity, and love for the nation 🚩✨.

There’s something about Dadar Chowpatty that just feels like home. It’s not 'fancy' like some of the other beaches, but that’s exactly why I love it.
I came here last Tuesday after a really long day at work, and honestly, it was exactly what I needed. I just sat on the sand for an hour, watched the waves, and looked at the Sea Link glowing in the distance. It’s one of those rare places in Mumbai where you can actually hear your own thoughts.
I ended up chatting with an old uncle who’s been coming here for 30 years, and he told me the beach has its own rhythm. You see families laughing, couples holding hands, and students stressed about exams—all just co-existing.
A few 'human' tips if you go:
• The Chana Chor Garam: Get a cone from the guy near the entrance. It’s the perfect salty snack for a walk.
• The Rocks: Be careful if you sit on the tetrapods! They’re great for photos, but they can be slippery.
• The Timing: Go right when the sun is dipping. The sky turns this incredible shade of pink and orange that no camera can really catch.
If you’re feeling a bit overwhelmed by the city pace, come here. Buy a kulfi, kick off your shoes, and just exist for a bit. It’s good for the soul. ❤️
